prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale:ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery;predictable latency,documented quality,retained interfaces;security:least-privilege,strong-authentication,segmentation,continuous audit—all environments. Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice):safety,commands,passes,anomalies,routing,handover;routine-operations authority;elevated access requires approved shift-role/time-limited need. Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs):authoritative accepted-orbits;controlled ephemerides/predictions→Mission Control Center,Mission Planning System,Payload Processing Facility;quality changes→archive operations queue before catalogue-validity updates. Mission Planning System(Cedar):authoritative observation/contact timelines;resource/slew/sun-angle/power/thermal/command/separation checks;command preparation package→Bluebell engineering;Laser Retroreflector Window constrained to approved interval. Network Control System(Lantern):authoritative circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact records;status→Bluebell;accepted-ephemeris pointing;approved routing between stations,processing,external interfaces;configuration changes logged;reject unreviewed transfer-time changes;Security Exception Ticket restricts transfer pending approved containment. Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters):assignments,availability,maintenance,staffing/site coordination;maintenance compatibility mandatory;antenna/link/site-service triage. Antenna Deicing Notice:mandatory pre-acquisition tasks. Spacecraft Operations Team:contingency margins,early maneuvers;Bluebell concurrence before uplink queue;safety triage;Pass Replay Packet verifies archived downlink supports anomaly reconstruction. North S-Band Antenna(nominal),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate):commands/telemetry→Bluebell;Kiruna X-Band Antenna,Svalbard X-Band Antenna:bulk downlink;all qualified tracking. Command Validation Gateway(Osprey):independent preapproval syntax/timing/range/sequence/mode/baseline/provenance/configuration/window checks;burns match screened plan;mask file requires matching integrity/configuration/operator-approval security baseline. Cybersecurity Desk:access/emergency/transfer exceptions;predeployment public-interface authentication/logging/abuse-control review;daily privileged-access review blocks dormant/shared/unexplained accounts;coordinates suspicious authentication/movement/behavior/tampering anomalies. Telemetry Ingest Service:state→command checks;validated frames/contact/flow/gaps→operations/engineering/processing;immutable raw staging;session

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
